title: Sponsorship FilterSet (report_type = 8)
description: Schema for the FilterSet payload of SPONSORSHIPS (8) reports — sponsorship deal tracking. Field names and types mirror the platform's FilterSet model 1:1 — no invented fields; unknown keys are rejected. The saved report's `filterset` JSON must conform to this schema.

_tl_source_of_truth.report_type_meaning: CAMPAIGN_MANAGEMENT — sponsorship/AdLink-level reporting. Filters are evaluated against a denormalized sponsorship dataset that already joins adlink, brand, channel, and organization. Direct joins from thoughtleaders_adlink to thoughtleaders_brand or thoughtleaders_channel are NOT possible — those FKs do not exist on the adlink table. See SKILL.md Step 2.V1 (Sponsorship reports section) for the canonical query shape.
_tl_source_of_truth.note: Same Django model as the intelligence schema, but only a subset of fields is meaningful for sponsorship reporting. Fields not listed here exist on the model but are inert for type 8.

channels.description: Restrict sponsorships to those involving specific channels. Resolve channel names → IDs via `tl channels find <name>` before emitting; never put channel names here.

brands.description: Restrict sponsorships to those involving specific brands. Resolve brand names → IDs via `tl brands find <name>` before emitting; never put brand names here.

days_ago.description: Rolling lower bound: only sponsorships with scheduled_date in the last N days.

createdat_from.description: AdLink created_at lower bound — when the deal entered the pipeline (NOT the publish date).

_tl_intent_hints: Default to 'sponsored_mentions' for type 8 unless the user specifically asks about organic mentions.

tl_sponsorships_only.description: Restrict to sponsorships TL sourced/managed (vs. organic/external sponsorship signals).

brand_approval.description: Narrows OPEN (publish_status 10) rows by the advertiser's per-party approval state. Comma list of PENDING/APPROVED/FINISHED or ints 1/2/3, plus 0/null/none for unset. Has no effect unless publish_status includes 10.

channel_approval.description: Narrows OPEN (publish_status 10) rows by the creator's per-party approval state. Same value forms as brand_approval. Has no effect unless publish_status includes 10.

agency_approval.description: Narrows OPEN (publish_status 10) rows by the agency's per-party approval state. Same value forms as brand_approval. Has no effect unless publish_status includes 10.

sort.description: Sortable column key from references/sortable_columns.json. Format: 'field' (asc) or '-field' (desc).

filters_json.description: Catch-all JSONField the platform interprets directly. For type 8 this is the primary place to encode publish_status, deal_status, price ranges, and any sponsorship-specific signals that don't have a first-class column on FilterSet.
_tl_intent_hints: publish_status: encode the user's intent ('matched', 'open', 'sold', 'live') here; the platform reads it.

ad_publish_status: live/currently-running intent uses string value '0' together with publish_status [3] — the platform interprets that combination as 'sold deals that are currently live' (filters to base-table publish_date IS NOT NULL).
Deal-stage filtering (matches → proposals → deals) goes through filters_json — there is no first-class status field on FilterSet.

committed: set committed '1' here to select committed deals (SOLD ∪ brand-approved OPEN); use it rather than AND-ing publish_status with brand_approval, which drops sold rows whose approval fields are unset.

_tl_rules: Type 8 ALWAYS needs a date scope. If the user gave no date hint at all, surface a follow-up question rather than silently defaulting — an unscoped type-8 report returns the entire AdLink table and is almost never what the user wanted. For vague-but-nonzero date language ('recent', 'lately', 'this year'), the `default_date_scope` intent override below applies the 365-day default with judgment.
Do NOT invent fields. Sponsorship status / publish_status / deal stage all live inside `filters_json` — encode them there, not as new top-level keys.

publish_status values are NUMERIC IDs from the set {3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10}, not string labels. See `report_glossary.md`'s 'Deal-stage jargon' table for the canonical user-phrase → ID mapping. The intent overrides below already use numeric IDs; never emit `publish_status: ['live']` or `['sold']` — those strings are not in the platform's enum.

Resolve brand/channel names → IDs via `tl brands find <name>` / `tl channels find <name>` BEFORE emitting `brands` / `channels` arrays. Type 8 with unresolved names is a hard failure mode — the saved report returns zero rows.

Keyword fields (`keywords`, `keyword_operator`, `content_fields`, `keyword_content_fields_map`, `keyword_exclude_map`) exist on the model but are inert for type 8 — sponsorships are filtered by relations, not content text. Do not emit them.
Topic fields (`topics`) are inert for type 8 — same reason. Do not emit.
Default `channel_formats: [4]` and `languages: ['en']` unless the user explicitly contradicts them.

live_only_intent._describes: Currently-running campaigns: the deal is sold AND the video has been published.

sold_only_intent._describes: Won deals only — regardless of whether the video has aired yet.

active_pipeline_intent._describes: Matched + open deals in motion (non-rejected, non-sold).

default_date_scope._describes: Vague-but-nonzero date language. Applies the 365-day default. NOT a fallback for queries with NO date hint at all — unscoped type-8 queries are rejected per `_tl_rules` rule #1.
